questions.question: A feature has the same value in every training row. What is its variance?
options: The number of rows
The target mean
questions.explanation: No row differs from the mean, so every squared deviation and the variance are zero.

questions.question: A binary target is generated by XOR of two centered binary features. Why might Pearson correlation with each feature be near zero?
options: XOR makes both features constant
Correlation can only be computed for continuous targets
Near-zero correlation proves that no model can use the features
The relationship is nonlinear even though the features jointly predict the target
questions.explanation: Each feature alone has no linear association with XOR, but their interaction is informative. Mutual information can detect dependence beyond linear correlation.

questions.question: Which description correctly contrasts filter, wrapper, and embedded selection?
options: Filter scores features independently, wrapper tests subsets with a model, embedded selects during model fitting
Filter always trains a deep model, wrapper ignores the target, embedded only removes constant columns
All three methods use the test set to choose the final subset
Wrapper selection never retrains a model after adding or removing a feature
questions.explanation: The methods differ in how closely selection is coupled to model fitting and in their computational cost.

questions.question: What does a sufficiently strong L1 penalty often do to an irrelevant feature's coefficient?
options: It forces the coefficient to equal one
It drives the coefficient exactly to zero
It makes the feature categorical
It copies the coefficient into the test set
questions.explanation: The absolute-value penalty has a sparsifying effect, so some fitted coefficients can become exactly zero.

questions.question: Why is recursive feature elimination usually more expensive than a variance filter?
options: A variance filter always trains one model per feature
RFE never examines model performance
RFE repeatedly fits a model while removing features, whereas variance filtering is a direct statistic
RFE can only be used with one feature
questions.explanation: RFE evaluates model rankings across several shrinking subsets; a variance filter needs no repeated predictive fits.

questions.question: Where should feature selection be fitted when estimating generalization?
options: On all rows before splitting, so the subset is stable
On the test labels after the model is trained
On the validation predictions only
On each training fold, with the held-out rows used only for evaluation
questions.explanation: Selecting with held-out outcomes leaks information and inflates the score. The selection step belongs inside the training pipeline.
